Diego / team,

Thanks for the draft schedule — we reviewed it with finance and a couple of follow-ups came up. CloudWorks expects a multiyear ramp and needs smoother monthly drawdown expectations so our monthly burn rate doesn’t spike against forecast. Specific asks: 

- Can you provide a laddered taper instead of the front-loaded Q1 draw? We need more consistent monthly credits in the first 9 months.
- We also need clarity on invoice ownership: will GCP invoice our billing contact directly or will Redwood provide a consolidated invoice we reconcile?
- Any attachments with a visual cadence (spreadsheet or chart) will help us present to procurement.

We can sign once the cadence is agreed — Procurement is ready to move next week.

Best,
Aaron

Subject: RE: RW-4729 - proposed cadence for GCP private offer redemption

Aaron — appreciate the quick read. Short answers up front and attached a revised laddering XLSX.

1) Laddered taper: yes — attached is a 12-month ladder that smooths Q1 into monthly increments (tab "Laddered_12mo"). It front-loads only 10% in month 1 then ramps to a steady cadence months 2–9, with a modest tail in months 10–12.

2) Invoice ownership: two options we support — (A) GCP invoices CloudWorks directly (standard GCP billing) or (B) Redwood issues a consolidated usage statement and invoice for the private-offer seat/commit portion and GCP invoices only the cloud usage. Procurement preference dictates which we pick. We can provide the invoice routing map to show who receives what.

3) Visuals: included invoice-routing-map.png and the XLSX with charts.

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm preferred invoice flow (Option A or B) by EOD Friday.
- If Option B, loop in your AP contact and we’ll send the consolidated invoice template for legal review.
- If you want a canary month (smaller draw) before full cadence, we can run that for month 1.

Attaching: RW-4729_commit_schedule_v2.xlsx, invoice-routing-map.png

Thanks,
Diego
